[Date]

Priority Health Appeals  
Fax: 616-975-8894

Re: Appeal of denial of prior authorization for cervical fusion  
Member: Skyler Mercado  
Member ID: W988378527  
Plan: Priority Health Commercial/ACA  
Reference number: POC-B7C7B913DC-54149  
Requested procedure: Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion, CPT 22551

To the Priority Health Appeals Department:

I am appealing Priority Health’s denial dated August 1, 2026, which determined that the requested cervical fusion does not meet the plan’s medical-necessity criteria. I request that Priority Health overturn the denial and approve the requested C5-C6 anterior cervical discectomy and fusion.

The clinical record supports medical necessity:

- I have had 18 months of progressive neck pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- I completed 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training, from April 12, 2026, through June 21, 2026. I completed 18 visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for six months without adequate relief.
- A cervical corticosteroid injection on May 22, 2026, provided only four weeks of partial relief.
- MRI performed on May 20, 2026, shows a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and compression of the C6 nerve root.
- I have radicular pain and numbness extending into the right thumb and index finger, together with weakness.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the MRI-documented level.
- The proposed procedure is directed at the documented C5-C6 structural abnormality and the corresponding C6 nerve-root compression.
- There is no active infection or untreated substance-use condition. I am a nonsmoker, with a BMI of 29, and the record does not identify an uncontrolled medical condition that would make surgery unsafe.
- The procedure was recommended by Marchetti, MD, an orthopedic surgeon.

This record demonstrates persistent and progressive symptoms, failure of appropriate conservative treatment, objective imaging findings, corresponding neurologic symptoms and weakness, and examination findings that correlate with the affected level. The proposed surgery is therefore a focused treatment for the documented C5-C6 pathology rather than treatment for nonspecific neck pain alone.

I understand that Priority Health identifies cervical fusion review under its Spine Procedures policy, Policy 91581-R23, and that the detailed clinical criteria are handled through TurningPoint. I am not quoting the plan’s policy because the detailed TurningPoint criteria applied to this request were not publicly available. Please provide, as part of this appeal:

1. The exact TurningPoint guideline and version used for this determination.
2. Every medical-necessity criterion Priority Health contends was not satisfied.
3. The clinical information reviewed by the decision-maker.
4. The specific clinical rationale for concluding that this request does not meet the applicable criteria.
5. Any additional records or information required to satisfy the applicable criteria.

Please have the request reviewed by a qualified clinician with relevant expertise in spine surgery or spinal disorders. I ask Priority Health to consider the enclosed clinical records, including the MRI report, physical therapy discharge note, medication and injection history, examination findings, and the surgeon’s documentation.

Please reverse the denial and authorize CPT 22551 for the indicated C5-C6 procedure. If Priority Health upholds the denial, please send a complete written explanation of the reasons, the criteria applied, the records relied upon, and all further appeal or external-review rights.

This appeal is being submitted within the 180-day appeal period stated in the denial notice, no later than January 28, 2027.

Sincerely,

Skyler Mercado  
Member ID: W988378527

[Telephone number]

- Orthopedic surgery clinical notes from Marchetti, MD
